question: With no new GPU budget yet, should the next investment be more supervised examples or another small GRPO run?
queries: DeepSeekMath Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models GRPO arxiv paper
DeepSeek R1 Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning cold start SFT arxiv
ReTool Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Tool Use in LLMs arxiv paper code interpreter

details: web.open (3 primary papers in one call)
web.find (six within-document lookups in one call)

recommendation: Spend the next scarce budget on human review of answer support and a small number of failure-targeted, verified supervised trajectories; defer another GRPO run. This is a priority for evidence collection and data curation, not a claim that adding examples will necessarily improve the model.

claims.text: DeepSeekMath GRPO replaces PPO’s learned value-model baseline with scores from multiple outputs to the same question.
DeepSeekMath’s reported RL phase used about 144,000 math questions and sampled 64 outputs per question.
ReTool trained a code-integrated cold-start SFT model before applying RL with interleaved code execution.
ReTool used a rule-based final-answer correctness reward against ground truth and did not include code executability in that reward.
DeepSeek-R1’s authors say reward reliability is central to RL and that reliable signals are hard to construct for open-ended tasks.
DeepSeek-R1’s authors report reward hacking with a helpfulness reward: reward rose while Codeforces performance fell.

baseline: Before training, compare the current v5 checkpoint with the same checkpoint given a compact, fixed few-shot prompt containing reviewed tool-use-and-evidence demonstrations. Keep the question set, corpus, decoding, and scoring identical; exclude test-question content from demonstrations.
matched_test: On the same frozen 40 development questions, blindly review answer support for the 20 answerable items, and record execution-error episodes, latency, and inference cost for all 40. Compare current v5 with the no-training few-shot baseline using paired question-level results. Reserve separate, unseen questions before any later SFT model is promoted; do not call the 40-question development result a held-out effect, or treat source span presence or replay success as answer correctness.
decision_rule: Predeclared development-pilot gate, not a significance claim: prioritize preparing a small targeted SFT dataset if the reviewed few-shot baseline improves supported-answer passes from v5’s 3/20 to at least 6/20 on the same answerable development items, loses none of the three currently passing items, keeps execution-error episodes at or below 1/40, and keeps median latency and inference cost each at or below 1.20× v5. Train when compute exists, then require a separately reserved matched held-out test before claiming model improvement. Reconsider GRPO only after a blinded audit shows a reliable reward that tracks supported-answer judgments on unseen outputs and a small matched rollout shows nontrivial reward variation; the numerical agreement/variation threshold for that future GRPO gate is explicitly unset pending labeled samples.
uncertainty: The 3/20 supported-answer counts are provisional, the sample is small, and no causal comparison of additional SFT versus GRPO exists for this specific Qwen3-8B reader. The cited math/tool-RL studies use different tasks, model scales, and verifiable ground-truth rewards, so their gains do not transfer directly. The proposed +3/20 threshold is a practical pilot rule rather than a statistical confidence bound.

question: For long papers, keep BM25 passage search or test hybrid retrieval plus reranking?
queries: site:arxiv.org long document question answering hybrid BM25 dense retrieval reranking paper
site:arxiv.org QASPER retrieval BM25 dense reranker evidence long scientific papers
QASPER dataset original paper evidence selection retrieval full scientific papers arxiv
recommendation: Keep BM25 as the shipping baseline and run an offline hybrid BM25+dense candidate test; add reranking only as a separately measured ablation, because domain mismatch can hurt.

claims.text: QASPER pairs full research papers with human-selected supporting evidence, allowing evidence retrieval to be evaluated separately from answer generation.
SciRet found hybrid retrieval more robust than sparse or dense alone in its scientific corpus, but its pseudo-relevance labels were derived from the hybrid system.
SciRet reported that an MS MARCO-trained cross-encoder reduced precision on its scientific corpus.
A QASPER study examined a retriever-ranker-reader pipeline and reported that stage choices affected answer quality.

baseline: Existing BM25 passage ranking, fixed passage segmentation and top-k/token budget.
matched_test: Use the same frozen papers/questions and human evidence sets. Compare BM25, BM25+dense fusion, and fusion+reranker at identical top-k and downstream context token budget; record full-evidence-set recall, answer support, per-query retrieval latency, index size, and memory.
decision_rule: Pilot only if hybrid improves complete human-evidence-set hit by at least 3 questions on 20 answerable cases, with no decrease in human-reviewed supported answers and retrieval p95 latency no more than 25% above BM25. Admit reranking only if it adds at least 2 further complete evidence hits without losing supported answers. Thresholds are local pilot choices.
uncertainty: The available studies use different corpora and models; SciRet labels risk favoring the hybrid system. Local evidence-hit and latency baselines are unset, so no production switch is justified yet.

question: For two concurrent Qwen3-8B readers, focus next latency test on prefix caching or speculative decoding?
queries: site:docs.vllm.ai automatic prefix caching only prefill shared prefix latency documentation
site:docs.vllm.ai speculative decoding inter token latency low QPS high QPS documentation
site:arxiv.org speculative decoding latency memory bound small batch large batch paper
recommendation: Test prefix caching first if the two readers reuse an identical serialized system/paper prefix; make prompt-prefix identity and cache-hit rate the first measurements. If real traffic shares little prefix or decode dominates, test speculative decoding next.

claims.text: vLLM prefix caching reuses KV cache for matching prefixes and reduces prefill work, but it does not reduce decoding time.
vLLM documents speculative decoding primarily as a way to reduce inter-token latency for medium-to-low-QPS, memory-bound workloads.
A serving study found speculative-decoding speedups often shrink as server load rises and depend on draft acceptance and model sizes.

baseline: Same Qwen3-8B serving stack with prefix caching disabled and speculative decoding disabled, two concurrent clients, frozen prompt and output-length distribution.
matched_test: On the same machine and two-client replay, alternate caching off/on after warmup with the same exact prompt bytes and decoding settings. Include a shared-prefix stratum and a deliberately distinct-prefix stratum. Record TTFT, inter-token latency, end-to-end p50/p95, output tokens, throughput, VRAM, and cache hits.
decision_rule: Pursue prefix caching if the shared-prefix stratum yields at least 20% lower median TTFT and at least 10% lower median end-to-end latency, with p95 end-to-end no worse than 10%, and the real workload exhibits at least 50% prefix reuse. Otherwise test speculative decoding under the same two-client load. These are predeclared local thresholds.
uncertainty: Actual prompt serialization, prefix overlap, prefill/decode split, hardware, and baseline latency are unset. Prefix caching offers no expected benefit for divergent prefixes; no speedup is assumed.

question: For paper QA, whole long paper or iterative selected-passage search/inspection?
queries: site:arxiv.org long document QA iterative retrieval reading selected passages versus full context paper
site:arxiv.org long context lost in the middle retrieval augmented generation long document QA
site:arxiv.org QASPER iterative search passages whole paper question answering evidence
recommendation: Keep iterative search and inspection of selected passages as the default paper-reading path, with a bounded ability to inspect neighboring sections and revisit search; test whole-paper input as a matched comparator on papers that fit context.

claims.text: Long-context model performance can degrade when relevant information sits in the middle of a long input.
A QASPER document-QA system explicitly separated text extraction, evidence retrieval, and answer generation and reported a 7.19 Answer-F1 gain over its baselines.
LongRAG argues that passage chunking can lose global context and noisy retrieval can obscure evidence, motivating some access to broader structure.

baseline: One whole-paper prompt with the same model, decoding, question, source text normalization, and maximum total input/output token cap wherever the paper fits.
matched_test: Replay the same answerable and unanswerable questions through whole-paper input and the current iterative search/read/extract path. For papers exceeding the limit, report a separate infeasible stratum rather than truncating silently. Blind-review atomic answer support, completeness, tool failures, tokens, and latency.
decision_rule: Retain iterative inspection if it yields at least 3 more supported answers on 20 answerable cases, or equal support with at least 25% fewer total input tokens, and does not add more than 1 execution-error episode on 40. Whole-paper wins only if it improves supported answers by at least 3 and fits at least 90% of the selected paper set within the configured context cap. These are pilot thresholds.
uncertainty: The studies are not a direct Qwen3-8B code-reader comparison. Retrieval misses, multi-section synthesis, and paper-length distribution may overturn the default; local token and latency measurements are unset.

question: With capacity to review ~100 more trajectories, prioritize teacher-generated traces or manually corrected failure cases?
queries: site:arxiv.org agent supervised fine tuning failure correction trajectories versus teacher demonstrations data selection
site:arxiv.org learning from mistakes self correction trajectory fine tuning agents teacher generated traces
site:arxiv.org data quality human corrected traces synthetic teacher trajectories agent training
recommendation: Prioritize manual correction of the reader’s own failed trajectories, especially unsupported answers with successful execution; retain the original failing prefix and add a verified recovery continuation. Use teacher traces only where they cover an unmet failure class and pass human evidence checks.

claims.text: ROSS argues historical rollouts contain mistakes and redundant actions that should not all be imitated, and applies supervision selectively.
Reflective Recovery turns failed prefixes into recovery examples and reports gains on mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
SCoRe found offline supervised correction traces can suffer distribution mismatch and behavior collapse, so corrected traces are not guaranteed to teach recovery.

baseline: Unfiltered teacher-generated successful traces, with a human verifying tool execution and answer evidence before any use.
matched_test: Use the 100-review budget on 50 reader failure cases and 50 teacher traces sampled from the same question/failure strata. Blindly score each for a novel, replayable, evidence-supported action/answer correction and annotation minutes. No training is required for this screening. If training later becomes available, compare equal-count SFT sets on frozen held-out questions.
decision_rule: Allocate subsequent annotation to corrected failures if at least 10 more of the 50 are novel, replayable, evidence-supported learning examples than the teacher arm, or if yield per annotation hour is at least 25% higher, with no increased rate of unsupported final answers in a later matched SFT test. These are local pilot thresholds.
uncertainty: No direct head-to-head study on this reader exists. Manual correction may be slow and can introduce annotator inconsistency; teacher traces may help novel tool paths. The cited correction studies concern different models/tasks and do not establish a local effect size.
